transport: TCP inside the authenticated WireGuard tunnel only
rules: WireGuard cryptokey routing authenticates the source /32 to an approved public key; never expose this port to LAN TCP or UDP
server sends preface plus a fresh random ticket; every H heartbeat or D disconnect must echo that stream ticket; A acknowledges
only a valid heartbeat installs a newer server-issued stream generation; delayed openings, messages and close events from superseded streams cannot change the new generation
a valid D marks presence offline without disabling, revoking or freeing the identity/address; the client then closes its tunnel even when acknowledgement fails
a missed heartbeat first means reconnecting; a managed peer with recent forwarded replies is degraded when control is unhealthy, unless it sent an authenticated goodbye
a server event may arrive after the first heartbeat is sent and before its acknowledgement; the client validates the ticket and handles that event immediately
legacy peers without presence use changes in authenticated inbound WireGuard bytes, including keepalives, with a 35-second monotonic lease; outbound bytes never renew presence
native status failure means unknown, not disappearance of authorization
all authorized records, including offline and disabled peers, consume the unchanged maximum-three capacity
server restart clears authorization and presence together; no stream ticket is reusable across endpoints
